controls.section: Operating system hardening > Operating system event logging
controls.text: Security-relevant events for Apple macOS operating systems are centrally logged.

controls.section: Operating system hardening > Operating system event logging
controls.text: Security-relevant events for Linux operating systems are centrally logged.

controls.section: Operating system hardening > Operating system event logging
controls.text: Security-relevant events for Microsoft Windows operating systems are centrally logged.

controls.section: Server application hardening > Server application event logging
controls.text: Security-relevant events for server applications on internet-facing servers are centrally logged.

controls.section: Server application hardening > Server application event logging
controls.text: Security-relevant events for server applications on non-internet-facing servers are centrally logged.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Security monitoring policy
controls.text: A security monitoring policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Centralised event logging facility
controls.text: A centralised event logging facility is implemented.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Centralised event logging facility
controls.text: Event logs sent to a centralised event logging facility are sent as soon as possible after they occur.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Centralised event logging facility
controls.text: Event logs sent to a centralised event logging facility are encrypted in transit using Australian Signals Directorate (ASD)-approved cryptography.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Centralised event logging facility
controls.text: Event logs are protected from unauthorised access.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Centralised event logging facility
controls.text: Event logs are protected from unauthorised modification and deletion.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Centralised event logging facility
controls.text: An accurate and consistent time source is used for event logging.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log details
controls.text: For each event logged, the date and time of the event, the relevant user or process, the relevant filename, the event description, and the information technology equipment involved are captured.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log details
controls.text: To the extent possible, event logs are captured and stored in a consistent and structured format.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Cyber security personnel have access to sufficient tools to facilitate the detection of cyber security events and the identification of cyber security incidents.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Cyber threat intelligence services are used to support the detection of cyber security events and the identification of cyber security incidents.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Suitable AI models are used to augment the detection of cyber security events and the identification of cyber security incidents.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Event logs from critical servers are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Event logs from internet-facing servers are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Event logs from non-internet-facing servers are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Event logs from workstations are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Event logs from security products are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Event logs from internet-facing network devices are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Event logs from non-internet-facing network devices are analysed in a timely manner to detect cyber security events.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log monitoring
controls.text: Cyber security events are analysed in a timely manner to identify cyber security incidents.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Threat hunting
controls.text: Threat hunting activities, informed by current strategic and sector-specific cyber threat intelligence, are conducted at least every three months.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log retention
controls.text: Event logs are retained in a searchable manner for at least 12 months.

controls.section: Security monitoring > Event log retention
controls.text: Event logs are retained as per minimum retention requirements for various classes of records as set out by the National Archives of Australia’s Administrative Functions Disposal Authority Express (AFDA Express) Version 2 publication.

controls.section: Software development fundamentals > Software event logging
controls.text: Security-relevant usage, error messages and crashes for software are centrally logged.

controls.section: Databases > Database event logging
controls.text:
Security-relevant events for databases are centrally logged, including:

- access or modification of particularly important content
- addition of new users, especially privileged users
- changes to user roles or privileges
- attempts to elevate user privileges
- queries containing comments
- queries containing multiple embedded queries
- database and query alerts or failures
- database structure changes
- database administrator actions
- use of executable commands
- database logons and logoffs.

controls.section: Network design and configuration > Network device event logging
controls.text: Security-relevant events for internet-facing network devices are centrally logged.

controls.section: Network design and configuration > Network device event logging
controls.text: Security-relevant events for non-internet-facing network devices are centrally logged.

controls.section: Identity and access management > Privileged access to systems
controls.text: Privileged access events are centrally logged.

controls.section: Identity and access management > Privileged access to systems
controls.text: Privileged user account and security group management events are centrally logged.

controls.section: Identity and access management > Multi-factor authentication
controls.text: Successful and unsuccessful multi-factor authentication events are centrally logged.

controls.section: Identity and access management > Single-factor authentication
controls.text: Successful and unsuccessful single-factor authentication events are centrally logged.

controls.section: Identity and access management > Unprivileged access to systems
controls.text: Use of unprivileged access is centrally logged.

controls.section: Identity and access management > Emergency access to systems
controls.text: Use of break glass accounts is centrally logged.

controls.section: Identity and access management > Third-party application access and device code authentication
controls.text: Consent grants, token issuance and token use for third-party OAuth applications are centrally logged.

controls.section: Software development fundamentals > Secure software development
controls.text: Software generates sufficient event logs to support the detection of cyber security events.

controls.section: Software development fundamentals > Secure software development
controls.text: Event logs produced by software ensure that any sensitive data is protected.

controls.section: Software development fundamentals > Network application programming interfaces
controls.text: Network API calls that facilitate modification of data, or access to data not authorised for release into the public domain, and are accessible over the internet, are centrally logged.

controls.section: Software development fundamentals > Network application programming interfaces
controls.text: Network API calls that facilitate modification of data, or access to data not authorised for release into the public domain, but are not accessible over the internet, are centrally logged.

controls.section: Software development fundamentals > Software interaction with databases
controls.text: All queries to databases from software, and any resulting crash or error messages, are centrally logged.

controls.section: Artificial intelligence application development > Excessive agency
controls.text: All tool invocations, external requests and outputs generated by agentic AI applications are centrally logged with sufficient detail to support cyber security incident investigations.

controls.section: Managed services and cloud services > Access to systems by service providers
controls.text: All access to an organisation’s systems by a service provider is independently logged by the organisation in a manner that the service provider cannot modify or delete, and analysed in a timely manner to detect any anomalous, unexpected or unauthorised activity.
